items.title: US business activity cools in October; strong demand fueling price pressures By Reuters
items.excerpt: WASHINGTON, Oct 23 (Reuters) - US business activity slowed modestly in October, though robust demand allowed companies to raise prices for goods and services, a sign that inflation could increase further and remain persistently high in the coming months. S&P Global said on Friday its flash US Composite PMI Output Index, which tracks the manufacturing and services sectors, slipped to 57.6 this month from a five-year high reading of 58.4 in September. A reading above 50 indicates expansion in the private sector. Strength in manufacturing was offset by a slight pullback in the vast services sector. The PMI suggested the economy started the fourth quarter on solid footing following what is expected to have been a strong performance in the July-September quarter. Economists expect the government’s advance gross domestic product report next week to show the economy growing at around a 3.0% annualized rate last quarter, mainly driven by consumer spending and business investment in AI. The economy has so far not shown any signs of buckling under the weight of the oil price shock stemming from the US-Israeli war with Iran, with savings, generous tax returns in the spring, tariff refunds, a strong stock market performance and corporate profits providing a cushion. Economists warned that the inflation fallout from the drawn-out Middle East conflict was likely to slow consumer spending this quarter. ... Its gauge of prices for output rose to 59.8, the highest reading since August 2022, from 58.4 in September. Businesses across manufacturing and services sectors raised prices. Delivery performance by suppliers to manufacturers deteriorated further. The survey’s measure of suppliers’ delivery times dropped to a more than four-year low of 38.1 from 40.9 in September. SUPPLY BOTTLENECKS INTENSIFYING "Cost pressures remain a key concern," said Chris Williamson, chief business economist at S&P Global Market Intelligence. "Supply chain bottlenecks have meanwhile intensified, and order book backlogs are growing, making it easier for companies to pass higher costs on to customers." ... Consumer and producer prices increased strongly in September, the government reported this month, raising concerns that inflation was fanning out across the economy. The Federal Reserve in September raised its overnight benchmark interest rate by 25 basis points to the 3.75%-4.00% range. ... Economists expect the US central bank to stand pat at its meeting next week and hike borrowing costs again in December.

Former President Obama is expected to make two Midwest trips to Cleveland, Ohio and Detroit, Mich. to help move the needle for Democrats in the two battleground states. Obama will first travel to Ohio to hold a rally with former Sen. Sherrod Brown (D-Ohio), who is locked in a tight battle with Ohio Republican Jon Husted for the Buckeye State’s Senate seat. According to The Hill’s partner Decision Desk HQ (DDHQ), Brown has a 51 percent chance to defeat Husted and is anticipated to be one of the tightest races in this year’s midterms. Following Obama’s Cleveland rally, he will travel north to Detroit to campaign with Michigan’s Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed, who is facing former Rep. Mike Rogers (R-Mich.). DDHQ has El-Sayed holding a steady lead over Rogers, 68 percent to 32 percent, respectively. ... Despite the Democrat frenzy, Trump is not done with his midterm tour. The president will hold a 7 p.m. rally in Perry Ga. in an attempt to boost Republican Senate candidate Rep. Mike Collins, who is going up against incumbent Democrat Sen. Jon Ossoff.

items.title: This US House district was once a political battleground. ...
items.excerpt: RALEIGH, N.C. -- In 2022, Democrat Wiley Nickel ran as a moderate and narrowly won North Carolina's 13th Congressional District by about 9,000 votes. Two years later, the current congressman, Republican Brad Knott, ran as a conservative and coasted into the U.S. House by more than 70,000 votes. ... Voters didn't change their minds. Politicians changed their voters. The Republican-controlled legislature redrew the state's congressional map to transform what was one of the last remaining swing districts in the South to a safe GOP seat. Lawmakers split the rectangular 13th District into an hourglass shape that carved out Democratic voters in Raleigh and replaced them with a swath of rural counties reaching up to the Virginia border. Swing seats, meaning a district that a presidential candidate won by 5 percentage points or fewer in the previous election, are disappearing from the national map. For decades after World War II, the number of competitive seats in the House slowly eroded as the United States grew more polarized, voters were less likely to split their ticket between parties and people moved closer to like-minded neighbors, creating Democratic strongholds in urban areas and Republicans ones across rural America. That decline accelerated over the past year after Republican President Donald Trump sparked a partisan redistricting battle. The number of swing districts fell from 45 to 37. There were 96 House seats that fit the modern definition of a swing seat in 1964, according to one count from the 1970s, when the shrinking number of such districts was first noted. That means the overwhelming majority of House seats are effectively won in primaries, with the support of only a fraction of voters who usually are at the extreme ideological end of their party.

items.title: Box Office: 'Clayface' Takes No. 1, 'You Can See Everything' Follows
items.excerpt: # Box Office: ‘Clayface’ Lands at No. 1 with $10.4 Million Debut, ‘You Can See Everything’ Adds $6.14 Million on Friday ... Clayface might have been a considerably nicher choice for a feature film than DC’s “Supergirl” and “Superman,” but that didn’t stop audiences from showing out to catch the Batman supervillain’s gory, nightmare-inducing origin story at the box office this weekend. ... The new release generated $10.4 million from 3,458 North American theaters on Friday, taking the No. 1 spot. It’s a strong start for the film, which looks to pull in $24 million by Sunday. Directed by James Watkins, “Clayface” follows the titular Batman villain, a rising movie star also known as Matt Hagen (Tom Rhys Harries), who volunteers for a highly experimental medical procedure after his face is severely disfigured. Naomi Ackie, David Dencik, Max Minghella and Eddie Marsan also star. Variety’s Guy Lodge called the film “its own ugly animal; perhaps the characters and conflicts introduced here would pall if given the franchise treatment, but in the context of a single, genre-melding romp, they’re fresh and ickily enjoyable.” ... A24’s much-hyped Elizabeth Holmes documentary “ You Can See Everything” landed in second place on Friday, making $6.14 million from 2,655 North American theaters, up from 855 at opening weekend. The buzzy doc has made $31.7 million domestically so far. Rival estimates suggest the film will gross another $20 million by Sunday. Comedian Nathan Fielder and “Primetime” filmmaker Lance Oppenheim quietly worked on the movie for more than three years, which offers an unhinged look at the Theranos founder a month before she began an 11-year prison sentence for defrauding investors. In addition to being eligible for best documentary feature at the 99th Academy Awards, the film will also be submitted across the board as seen on A24’s awards site: best picture, director, production design, cinematography, costume design, film editing, makeup and hairstyling, sound and original score. Laika’s “ Wildwood,” another new release, landed in third place on Friday, grossing $4.28 million from 2,942 North American theaters. Featuring a voice cast that includes Carey Mulligan, Jacob Tremblay and others, the stop-motion film looks to bring in $11.2 million by Sunday. Directed by Travis Knight, “Wildwood” revolves around a teenage girl who travels with a classmate into an enchanted forest after her brother is abducted. Strong reviews should continue to propel the lavish film at the box office, which carries a substantial $100 million price tag. Black Bear’s “ Wicker” followed in fourth place, earning $2.36 million on Friday from 1,471 North American theaters. The offbeat romantic comedy, directed by Eleanor Wilson and Alex Huston Fischer, is targeting a $5.5 million opening weekend. Described as an “audacious comedic fable,” “Wicker” tells the love story of an ostracized fisherwoman (Olivia Colman) who commissions a husband from the local basketmaker (Peter Dinklage). Alexander Skarsgård plays said husband. Elizabeth Debicki also stars. ... Coming in fifth was Legendary Entertainment’s “Street Fighter.” The action film grossed $2.34 million on Friday and should add another $8.4 million by Sunday, bringing its cumulative gross to $46.7 million. ... “Street Fighter,” directed by Kitao Sakurai, stars Noah Centineo and Andrew Koji as two estranged fighters in the 90s who are recruited to enter a tournament that forces them to face off against each other.

The Band Turnstile holds the Grammys for Best Rock Album - NEVER ENOUGH and Best Metal Performance - BIRDS at the 68th Grammy Awards in Los Angeles, CA, Sunday, Feb. 1, 2026. Turnstile is tonight's Musical Guest. The Baltimore rockers whose genre-bending sound incorporates elements of melodic hardcore, metal, and pop, will take the stage for the first time. Turnstile, formed in 2010, will perform their single "Birds" and a medley of "I Care" and "Dull," all tracks from their latest studio album, Never Enough. The band is currently in the middle of their The Never Enough Tour Pt. 2, playing venues across the United States before heading overseas next year for stops across Europe.

Following his historic, sold-out three-night run at Yankee Stadium, JAŸ-Z and Roc Nation have announced second stadium shows in London and Los Angeles due to unprecedented fan demand, expanding one of the year's most highly anticipated series of global performances. The Yankee Stadium run shattered the venue's all-time concert attendance records across all three nights and made JAŸ-Z the first artist ever to sell out three consecutive shows at the venue. A second Los Angeles show has also been added for Saturday, October 24, 2026 at SoFi Stadium, following the previously announced October 23 performance. These must-see performances celebrate JAŸ-Z's remarkable 30-year career and iconic catalog that has shaped music and culture around the world.
